item.description: Status of work on railway stations and bus stops in Switzerland updated according to the Federal Office of Transport.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 1168 railway stations accessible by the end of 2025 - 83 per cent of travelers benefit from the adaptations - 50 per cent of bus stops can be used - 250 million francs for 2025–2028
## Key facts - Publication → 29 September 2026 - Authority → Federal Office of Transport (UFT) - Railways → 1168 out of approximately 1800 stations and stops - Buses → approximately 25 000 stops - Obligation → Disability Act (LDis), by the end of 2023 - Planning by the end of 2029 → 193 stations and stops - Funding 2025–2028 → 250 million francs - Condition → proportionate intervention
On 29 September 2026, from Bern, the Federal Office of Transport (UFT) indicated in its latest report on the progress of the work that, at the end of 2025, people with disabilities could independently use 1168 of the approximately 1800 railway stations and stops in Switzerland. This figure is up by 36 from the previous year.
### Railways: passenger figures
The number of adapted stations does not correspond to the share of passengers affected. The larger stations were the first to undergo structural modernization: as a result, the renovations carried out to meet the needs of people with disabilities could be used by 83 per cent of all passengers. Current planning provides for another 193 stations and stops to be adapted by the end of 2029, with the share of benefiting passengers expected to rise to at least 87 per cent.
Under the Disability Act (LDis), railway companies and the owners of the roads had to renovate their stations and stops by the end of 2023 so that people with disabilities could use them independently. However, this obligation was subject to the proportionality of the intervention.
The UFT monitors implementation and requires interim measures for delayed projects, ensuring a uniform and proper assessment of proportionality. For the period 2025–2028, the Confederation has also allocated 250 million francs to supplement the basic funding.
For the first time, the report also examines the approximately 25 000 bus stops, which fall under the responsibility of the owners of the respective roads: Cantons, Cities and Municipalities. Fifty per cent can be used by passengers with reduced mobility; in some cases independently, in others with the assistance of staff. Forty-two per cent are inaccessible and require alternative measures, generally a shuttle service provided by the transport company to the nearest stop compliant with the LDis.
The report also records the difficulties that Cantons, Cities and Municipalities encounter in implementation: limited space and sloping terrain, conflicts with other land uses, complex procedures and delays caused by objections. DCPA, UCS and ACS support the authorities with documentation and knowledge transfer. This is the distinction that anyone using mezzi pubblici must bear in mind when reading the progress of the work. ## Two networks, two levels of accessibility
The comparison between the number of stations and the share of passengers should not be read as a single percentage. Railways and buses have different responsibilities and operating conditions, and the source distinguishes between independent use, staff assistance and replacement measures.
### Why the comparison matters
| Network | Status observed | Operational consequence | |---|---|---| | Rail | 1168 out of approximately 1800 can be used independently | 83 per cent of passengers can benefit from the works | | Buses | 50 per cent usable; 42 per cent inaccessible | Staff assistance or shuttle, as applicable |
The comparison shows that the national figure answers two different questions: how many stations and stops have been adapted, and how many passengers can benefit from the interventions. In rail transport, the initial modernization of the larger stations explains why the share of passengers is high compared with the total number of facilities. Planning through 2029, with another 193 adaptations, therefore measures the progress of the works and not a change that has already been implemented.
For buses, the 50 per cent figure brings together different situations. A stop may be used independently or require staff assistance; where it is inaccessible, the replacement measure indicated is generally a shuttle operated by the transport company to the nearest stop compliant with LDis. For people who use mezzi pubblici, the difference between independent use, assistance and shuttle is therefore a tangible part of interpreting the figure.
The responsible parties also differ. Railway companies are tasked with adapting railway stations and stops, while for bus stops the responsibility lies with the road owners, namely Cantons, Cities and Municipalities. The report notes that legal requirements have been incorporated into plans and processes, but limited space, sloping terrain, conflicts with other land uses, complex procedures and objections can slow down systematic and timely implementation.
Additional federal funding supports the 2025–2028 period, while the target of 87 per cent concerns rail planning by the end of 2029. These are therefore two time horizons that should not be confused when assessing the status of a national or cantonal network.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to use the report information
The most straightforward way to translate the national framework into a practical check is to proceed by stop type and accessibility level. The railway sector has a report and an implementation list; for buses, the report introduces for the first time a snapshot of the approximately 25,000 stops and indicates the responsible entities.
### Four practical steps
1. Identify the network. Determine whether the point to be used is a railway station/stop or a bus stop. This distinction determines which part of the report to consult and which responsibility to consider.
2. Check the railway. For railway stations and stops, the reference point is the 2026 Status Report with its attached list of DDA implementation status. This document allows users to read the framework of adjustments reported by the FOT without confusing the number of facilities with the passenger share.
3. Read the bus category. For a bus stop, responsibility lies with the road owner, namely the Canton, City, or Municipality. The data must be distinguished between autonomous use, staff assistance, and non-accessible stops. In the latter case, the generally provided replacement measure is the transport company's shuttle service to the nearest DDA-compliant stop.
4. Monitor delays and deadlines. When a railway project is delayed, the FOT requires transitional measures. The planning to keep an eye on extends until the end of 2029, while the Confederation's additional funding covers the 2025–2028 period. For the DDA, the original deadline for adjustments was the end of 2023, subject to the condition of proportionality of the intervention.
### The role of the authorities
Cantons, Cities, and Municipalities have integrated legal requirements into their plans and processes, but they must manage tight spaces, sloping terrain, conflicts with other land uses, complex procedures, and delays due to objections. The Swiss Conference of Cantonal Ministers of Public Works, Spatial Planning and Environment (BVPK), the Swiss Association of Cities (Städteverband), and the Swiss Association of Municipalities (Gemeindeverband) continue to support them with documentation and knowledge transfer. The report also plans to complement the quantitative data with best practice models aimed at the general public.

## In brief - Switzerland has ranked first since 2011 - Sweden and the United States complete the podium - China enters the top ten for the first time - The index uses 80 indicators and covers nearly 140 countries
## Key facts - Organization → WIPO - Edition → 18th - Indicators → 80 - Countries examined → nearly 140 - First place → Switzerland, since 2011 - Podium → Switzerland, Sweden, United States - New development → China among the top ten nations
### The Confederation's top spot GENEVA - Switzerland remains the world's most innovative country according to the ranking published each year by the World Intellectual Property Organization, WIPO. The Confederation has held first place since 2011, a position confirmed in this 18th edition as well.
The podium is unchanged from last year: Sweden and the United States rank behind Switzerland. They are followed by South Korea, noted as having risen from sixth place, Singapore and the United Kingdom. The ranking continues with Finland, the Netherlands, Denmark and China. For China, this is the first time it has been among the top ten nations.
The result is not built on a single parameter. The index examines 80 indicators and scrutinizes nearly 140 countries. The elements considered include spending on research and development, venture capital transactions, high-tech exports and filings of applications for intellectual property rights.
### WIPO's interpretation WIPO Director Daren Tang links the fastest progress to countries that regard innovation as a driver of resilience, growth and competitiveness. In his assessment, innovation ecosystems must be supported and nourished by thoughtful policies, significant investment and cross-sector collaboration. This is the interpretive lens offered by the organization alongside the ranking.
The reference to continuity since 2011 distinguishes Switzerland's result from a simple one-year leap. At the same time, China's presence in the top ten signals a change in the composition of the leading group, while South Korea's rise from sixth place highlights movement at the top of the list.
The framework therefore makes it possible to read three separate pieces of information: Switzerland's position, the comparison with the podium and the breadth of the scope used to calculate the index. The source does not present a single project or a specific sector as the exclusive explanation for the top position. ## How to read the result in Switzerland
### An index, not a single parameter For those who live or work in Switzerland, the practical point of the news is to understand that first place describes an overall position. The text does not identify it as the result of a single activity, a single company or a single sector. WIPO combines 80 indicators and applies them to nearly 140 countries: the ranking therefore offers a broad picture, while the source does not detail the weight of each item in Switzerland's result.
| Area observed | Data indicated by the source | |---|---| | Research and development | Expenditure on research and development | | Venture capital | Venture capital transactions | | High technology | High-technology exports | | Intellectual property | Filings of applications for intellectual property rights |
This distinction serves to avoid reducing innovation to technological products alone. Research and development is considered through spending; venture capital through transactions; high technology through exports; intellectual property through application filings. These are categories included in the calculation, not automatic results that the source attributes to every company or worker.
The international comparison should be read with the same caution. Switzerland is ahead of Sweden and the United States in the overall ranking, but the source does not state that it is first in each of the 80 indicators. ### Four reading steps 1. Start with the scope. Identify the ranking as WIPO's annual index, now in its 18th edition and compiled by examining nearly 140 countries. This immediately clarifies that it is an international comparison.
2. Check the numerical basis. The ranking is not based on a single figure: it refers to 80 indicators. Therefore, read the items cited by the source together, from research and development spending to applications for intellectual property rights, including venture capital and high-tech exports.
3. Separate continuity from changes. Switzerland's first place has been recorded since 2011; the podium with Sweden and the United States is the same as the previous year. South Korea's rise and China's entry into the top ten should be noted as separate elements.

item.description: Lindt&Sprüngli cuts the 2026 organic growth forecast to 0-2 percent and is considering broader price reductions from January after the impact of cocoa and summer heat.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Organic growth in 2026 falls to 0-2 percent - Previous target was 4-6 percent - Lindt is considering broader reductions from January - The share price fell to 7960 francs
## Key facts - Organic growth in 2026 → 0-2 percent - Previous target → 4-6 percent - Broader reductions → starting in January - Morning share price → 7960 francs, -6,9 percent - Target from 2028 → annual organic growth of 6-8 percent
### The new scenario for Lindt In Zurich, Lindt&Sprüngli revised its revenue target downward for the second time. For 2026, the organic growth forecast is now between 0 and 2 percent, compared with the 4-6 percent indicated so far. At the beginning of the year, the company was still targeting 6-8 percent; that target was abandoned in March.
The announcement was made on Tuesday. The rationale combines two factors: price increases made necessary by rising cocoa prices and the heat wave that hit Europe during the summer. With high temperatures, consumers showed less interest in Lindor balls and pralines.
> “No one felt like entering a specialty chocolate shop at 37 degrees,” said CEO Adalbert Lechner.
The increases, according to the company’s explanation, could not be avoided. After an initial decline, cocoa prices rose again and, even after the price adjustments, weighed on the gross margin. Lindt also intends to act on costs, while job cuts are not under discussion.
The raw materials situation then eased somewhat. Lindt is therefore considering broader reductions starting in January, with the aim of obtaining a greater volume of orders for next Easter and the Christmas period. The company says it is confident about the coming months and 2027. For those living in Switzerland, the topic becomes part of the reading of costo della vita in Svizzera, without the communication turning the assessment into a generalized promise.
The group also maintains its goal of improving the EBIT margin by 20-40 basis points in 2026. For 2027, it expects renewed volume growth, supported by an adapted pricing strategy, greater investment in the brand and falling cocoa prices. Financial forecasts for 2027 will be published in the first quarter; from 2028, annual organic revenue growth of 6-8 percent remains confirmed, with an annual improvement in the EBIT margin of 20-40 basis points. ## What changes for those who buy and those who watch the stock market
### Prices, sales channels and confidence The first practical point for those living in Switzerland is to distinguish what has already been done from what Lindt is still considering. Some reductions have been applied in Switzerland and Germany; a broader measure is instead indicated as possible from January. This distinction avoids reading as a certain price cut a decision that the company still presents as under consideration.
| Step | Reported signal | Practical reading | | Reductions already made | Switzerland and Germany | Observe the price applied | | From January | Possible broader reductions | Check for any change | | Easter and Christmas | Goal of more orders | Monitor demand's response |
The place of purchase also factors into the reading of the data. Demand declined mainly in specialty stores, while the decline was less pronounced in supermarkets. For the Swiss market, the news therefore does not describe identical behavior in every channel: it links sales weakness to the heat, but signals a different impact between specialty stores and supermarkets.
For an individual or family's budget, the point is not to turn Lindt's forecast into savings that can already be quantified. The company speaks of somewhat more relaxed raw-material prices and a strategy aimed at recovering volumes; the benefit for buyers will depend on the concrete application of the reductions. For the reader, the decline in the share price measures the market's reaction to the revenue warning, not the price of a single package.

The distinction is between reductions already implemented and measures that Lindt is still examining.
2. Use the occasions indicated by the company as checkpoints. The next Easter and the Christmas period are the windows during which Lindt wants to obtain a greater volume of orders. item.title: Lindt revises downwards its sales forecasts for 2026
item.description: Lindt expects revenue growth of 0%-2% (versus previous 4-6%), BP -8% in the morning, YTD performance -30%, -35% over 12 months, -24% over 5 years; headquarters in Kilchberg ZH, 15'500 employees.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Lindt expects turnover growth of between 0% and 2% - The previous estimate was 4-6% - The BP fell 8% in the morning - Seasonal orders are below expectations
## Key facts - Expected growth → 0%-2% of turnover - Previous estimate → 4-6% - Morning BP decline → 8% - Performance since the beginning of January → -30% - Performance over twelve months → -35% - Performance over five years → -24% - Headquarters → Kilchberg (ZH) - Workforce → 15'500 employees
### The revision of estimates
For the second time this year, Lindt & Sprüngli has revised its sales forecasts downward. The group now expects turnover growth of between 0% and 2%, compared with the 4-6% previously forecast. The revision comes after price increases initially caused by the surge in cocoa costs: consumer reaction was stronger than expected.
Keystone-ATS reports that price sensitivity and moderate consumer confidence have reduced order volumes, especially in the seasonal segment. The statement cites Germany, Switzerland and Austria.
> «Rather moderate consumer confidence and greater price sensitivity have resulted in order volumes below expectations, especially in the seasonal sector, particularly in Germany, Switzerland and Austria,» the statement reads.
Lindt also points to the wave of extreme heat that affected Europe during the summer: according to the company, it had a negative impact on revenues across the entire sector. Growth is instead described as solid in North America and Asia.
CEO Adalbert Lechner maintains that the decline in the price of cocoa from historic highs should gradually bring cost pressures back to normal. The company expects a recovery in demand and identifies 2027 as the year in which positive volume growth will be achieved, supported by pricing strategy, investments in brands, innovation and cost discipline.
On the stock market, the participation certificate, the BP, fell as much as 8% in the morning, while the market was generally oriented toward a fractional rise. The BP entitles holders to a dividend but not to voting rights and is the reference security for analysts. The indicated price is around 7970 francs; the security belongs to the SLI, which comprises the 30 most important stocks.
Performance is negative by 30% since the beginning of January, by 35% over twelve months and by 24% over five years. Lindt, backed by a 180-year tradition, has twelve of its own plants in Europe and the United States and 620 stores. In 2025 it generated turnover of 5,9 billion francs, up 8% thanks to strong price increases. ## How to read the signal in Switzerland
### Prices, volumes and markets
For those living in Switzerland, the most concrete indicator is the relationship between price and quantity sold. Lindt recorded revenue growth in 2025 thanks to strong price increases, but now reports orders below expectations for seasonal products. This alone does not prove that every price increase reduces demand, but it shows that price sensitivity has become an explicit variable in the group's estimates. Those tracking the cost of living in Switzerland can use this case as a company-specific indicator, without turning it into a general measure of prices.
The geography of demand changes the interpretation. Germany, Switzerland and Austria are the markets cited for the slowdown in seasonal orders; North America and Asia, by contrast, show solid growth. Extreme heat in Europe is a second factor identified by the company and concerns the revenues of the entire sector. The signal, therefore, is not uniform: it contains one component linked to prices and another connected to summer conditions.
| Signal | How to interpret it | |---|---| | Cocoa prices lower than historical highs | Cost pressures should gradually normalize | | Seasonal orders below expectations | Consumers' price sensitivity weighs on forecasts | | Growth in North America and Asia | Weakness is not described in all markets | | Target for 2027 | The company expects positive volume growth |
### The point for those watching the stock
For investors, the revision also matters for the credibility of forecasts. Jean-Philippe Bertschy, an analyst at Vontobel, warns that the second cut of the year weakens confidence in Lindt's ability to formulate accurate estimates. According to the comment, that ability had contributed to the stock's high valuation.
The question to follow is the one indicated by the analyst himself: does consumers' reaction to the increases reflect a structural problem of price elasticity or an isolated episode? In the first scenario, pricing power, long considered a strength of Lindt, remains under pressure. In the second, the normalization of cocoa costs and a recovery in demand may support the trajectory announced for 2027. These are interpretations anchored in the statements reported, not a new forecast.
The nature of the BP should also be kept distinct. The instrument recognizes the dividend, but not the vote; this is why it is the reference followed by analysts in the source. Its price movement should therefore be read together with the company's operating indications, not as a direct measure of households' chocolate purchases. To explore the impact of prices on the balance sheet, consult costo della vita in Svizzera.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## Procedure for the reader
### Five checks before drawing a conclusion
To use the press release as a reading tool, it is not enough to stop at the stock market movement. Follow these five steps, all based on the data provided by the company and the analyst's note.
1. Set the comparison. Put the new range 0%-2% next to the previous 4-6%. The first figure describes the current expectation for revenue growth; the second shows how much the forecast has been reduced.
2. Separate the factors. Keep distinct the spike in cocoa that had driven price increases, consumer sensitivity, seasonal orders and extreme heat in Europe. The source presents them as different elements of the revision.
3. Check the geographical area. Germany, Switzerland and Austria are associated with orders below expectations; North America and Asia with solid growth. This step avoids interpreting the slowdown as uniform across all markets.
4. Read the right security. The BP is entitled to the dividend but not to voting rights and is the reference for analysts. Therefore, compare its change in the morning with the periods since the beginning of January, twelve months and five years, without confusing the share price with sales volume.
5. Keep the two horizons separate. On the one hand, there is the CEO's expectation of positive volume growth in 2027; on the other, Vontobel's question about price elasticity, whether structural or isolated. Those looking at the scale of employment can pair the data on 15'500 employees and 620 stores with the search for aziende che assumono.

item.title: Swiss workers use AI, but few see its benefits
item.description: 28% of Swiss workers use generative AI every day, but only 10% see improved work quality. Findings from PwC research.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 28% use generative AI every day in Switzerland - Only 10% see improved work quality - 14% feel more motivated or confident - Up to 9% believe that AI fosters skills and creativity
## Key facts - Research → «Hopes and Fears» 2026 by PwC - Swiss sample → 1000 employees - Period → between May and June - Daily use of generative AI → 28% - Global average of daily use → 22% - Clear improvement in work quality → 10% - Motivation or confidence thanks to AI → 14% - Skills and creativity fostered by AI → up to 9%
28% of Swiss workers use generative AI every day, compared with the global average of 22%. This figure comes from the 2026 edition of the «Hopes and Fears» research conducted by PwC, which describes a cautious relationship with artificial intelligence tools: in Switzerland, usage is higher than the international average, but perceived benefits remain limited.
Only 10% of respondents see a clear improvement in work quality. 14% say they feel more motivated or confident thanks to these tools. Up to 9% believe that AI fosters skills and creativity, while 22% say it helps them manage more complex tasks. The data show a gap between frequency of use and perceived benefit.
### Frequent use, less clear benefits
The figure should be read on two levels. On the one hand, the 28% indicates daily use by a portion of the Swiss sample. On the other, the percentages for quality, motivation, skills, creativity and complex tasks indicate that using the tool is not automatically associated with a better result. In the text, the proposed response involves support and targeted training, not daily use alone.
Teena Madhvani, an executive at PwC Svizzera, argues that job security and salary are not enough to attract and retain talent. Trust, flexibility, a strong corporate culture and transparent development opportunities are also needed. To make AI truly useful, she adds, support and targeted training are necessary.
For the 2026 edition, 1000 employees in Switzerland were interviewed between May and June. Globally, approximately 50'000 active workers in 48 countries participated in the research. The Swiss sample is therefore part of a broader survey, which places the national figure alongside the global average for the use of generative AI. ## Security today, future skills
The second section of the research shifts the focus from the use of AI to the perception of job stability. 66% of Swiss workers feel secure in their jobs for the next twelve months, but only 27% are optimistic about demand for their skills three years from now. The gap between the two time horizons indicates that immediate security does not coincide with confidence in the future marketability of one’s skills.
Another signal concerns trust. 21% trust their direct supervisor and 17% top management, while only 19% say they clearly know which skills will be required in the future. The perceived problem therefore concerns not only technology: it also includes the relationship with the hierarchy and the ability to orient oneself toward what will be needed.
### The signals that influence the choice of a job
| Indicator | Result | |---|---| | Negative culture as a reason to reject a job | 54% | | Opposition to greater control in the workplace | 40% |
The 54% share indicates that a culture perceived as negative can become a reason to reject a job. The 40% instead signals the limit placed on control in the workplace. Together, the two shares describe a demand for trust and room for autonomy.
For those reading annunci di lavoro, the practical implication is to look beyond security and salary: the source identifies trust, flexibility, a strong culture and transparent development as elements capable of attracting and retaining talent. The comparison with aziende che assumono can therefore start from these criteria, without reducing the choice to compensation alone.
The same message applies to the introduction of AI. Technology is perceived as useful when accompanied by support and targeted training. For organizations, the research therefore brings together two dimensions: making the tools usable and making the career path clear. For workers, this means evaluating tasks, future skills and the quality of the environment together.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## From research to a personal assessment
The survey can become a personal assessment framework. It is not enough to ask only whether AI is being used: it is necessary to separate usage from the perceived effect and from the conditions that make it useful. The steps follow the themes indicated by the research.
### Four operational steps
1. **Map the tasks.** Distinguish the activities in which AI helps manage more complex tasks from those in which no clear improvement in quality can be seen. The question is not how often the tool is used, but what result is recognized.
2. Verify the support. Ask whether targeted support and training are available to make AI truly useful. The source identifies these two elements as necessary, so they should be considered together with everyday adoption.
3. Check the skills. Compare current activities with the skills that are expected to be required in the future. If the picture is unclear, the research shows that visibility into development remains an open issue.
4. Assess environment and autonomy. In a current job or a new one, examine company culture, flexibility, autonomy, trust, and level of control. These are the factors that the research places alongside security and salary.
For those considering new opportunities, this assessment prevents them from focusing on just one factor. For those already employed, it provides a framework for focusing the comparison on training, support, trust, and transparent development. The same framework makes it possible to distinguish frequent use of AI from use perceived as truly useful, without confusing adoption with results.
To connect this assessment to monthly income, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: The Swiss are the richest in the world
item.description: Switzerland ranks first for gross financial wealth per capita at 406'060 euros. According to Allianz's Global Wealth Report 2026, net wealth per person stands at 275'980 euros.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Switzerland first for gross financial wealth per capita - Second for net wealth, behind the United States - Global financial wealth rises to 268'400 billion
- Gross wealth per capita → 406'060 euros - Net wealth per capita → 275'980 euros - Global financial wealth → 268'400 billion euros - Study → Global Wealth Report 2026, Allianz - Compilation → end of 2025
### The report's ranking
406'060 euros in gross financial assets per capita make Switzerland the richest country in the world according to the Global Wealth Report 2026. The figure, referring to the end of 2025, is equivalent to almost 384'000 francs at the current exchange rate. To read the conversion between euros and francs, comparatore CHF/EUR can be used, while keeping the original figure distinct from the conversion indicated in the source.
The top spot does not apply to net wealth, however. Once liabilities are taken into account, Switzerland drops to second place, with 275'980 euros, almost 261'000 francs per person. The net ranking is led by the United States. The difference between gross assets and net wealth explains why the international position changes when financial obligations are included in the calculation.
The report was prepared by Allianz at the end of 2025 and has reached its 17th edition. In the meantime, global financial wealth has reached 268'400 billion euros, with an increase of 8,6% in one year. The authors attribute this in part to price gains in capital markets and the advance of artificial intelligence: funds and shares thus become a decisive factor in the ownership of wealth.
“Since 2019, nominal financial wealth has grown by 50%, but in real terms, that is, net of inflation, the increase is only 23%,” says Ludovic Subran, chief economist of Allianz, quoted in a press release. In Western Europe, real wealth is just 0,5% above the 2019 level. North America and China show stronger dynamics, respectively +21% and +70%.
The composition of investments also explains the new distribution of wealth. In 2025, securities grew by 12,4%, more than twice as much as bank deposits, which rose by 5,7%, and insurance and pensions, which increased by 5%. The share of securities in global wealth thus reached a record 46,9%. The North American figure is even more pronounced: 60,7% of household portfolios is invested in securities, and the region accounted for 51,4% of global wealth growth. Over the past ten years, increases in value explained 71% of the growth in North American financial wealth, compared with 36% in Western Europe. For researchers, therefore, not only how much is saved matters, but also how savings are invested. ## Comparison with the Swiss portfolio
For those living in Switzerland, the national breakdown shows more moderate growth than the global markets, but a gradually greater presence of securities. In 2025, households' gross financial wealth increased by 4% and reached 3'600 billion euros. The pace remained below Western Europe's 4,5% and far below the global 8,6%. The comparison describes Swiss households as a whole and not the result of a single individual position.
### More securities, but a share still below average
In the Swiss portfolio, securities recorded the strongest increase, at 9,7%. Bank deposits grew by 1,9%, while insurance and pensions recorded 1,1%. The share of securities rose from 30,9% to 32,6%, but remains below Western Europe's 36,8% and the global 46,9%. Insurance and pensions remain the main investment class, at 37,9%. Those who want to isolate the deposit component can examine conti bancari in Svizzera more closely, without confusing it with total financial wealth.
### The destination of new investments
New investments increased by 4,8%, reaching 94,0 billion euros. The distribution was relatively even: 35,7% in securities, 34,2% in insurance and pensions, 30,2% in bank deposits. Households focused primarily on funds, with purchases of 37,7 billion euros, the second-highest figure in the historical series. The figure suggests that the allocation decision accompanies wealth growth: the amount invested is not concentrated in a single class.
### The difference between nominal, real and net
Measured net of inflation, Swiss financial wealth grew by 3,9%; since 2019, the increase has been 13,3%, compared with Western Europe's 0,5%. Liabilities rose by 3,1%, to 1'200 billion euros, thus less than gross financial wealth. The ratio of liabilities to gross wealth fell from 32,3% to 32,0%, that is, about 32%, while net wealth increased by 4,5%, to 2'500 billion euros.
Taken together, these indicators show why gross, net and real wealth answer different questions: the first measures assets, the second takes obligations into account, and the third subtracts inflation. For a practical reading, the most appropriate comparison is therefore between like-for-like measures and between the structure of the Swiss portfolio and European and global benchmarks. ## What to observe in 2026
The report also offers a framework for reading 2026 without mistaking a forecast for an achieved result. Analysts estimate that global financial wealth will grow by 9% in 2026. The medium-term scenario is more challenging, however: weaker economic growth, persistent inflationary pressure, increasing geopolitical fragmentation and high public debt may weigh on return prospects.
### A four-step check
1. Distinguish the potential boost. Artificial intelligence may increase productivity and corporate profits, supporting capital market returns. The same dynamic, however, ties household wealth more closely to AI-driven equity markets and increases its vulnerability.
2. Measure the shock. According to calculations by Allianz, a 25% correction in the US S&P 500 index would destroy approximately 27'000 billion dollars, equivalent to 22'400 billion francs, of US household wealth in the year of the shock.
3. Compare the damage. The loss would be equivalent to almost 14% of the total net worth of US households. A decline of this magnitude would weigh on confidence and consumption and push the US economy into recession.
4. Look at ownership. Katharina Utermöhl, an Allianz specialist, notes that the decisive question is who owns the assets and participates in the returns. If value creation through AI were to pass mainly through capital, her analysis suggests that broader participation in returns and measures to support workers through the transition would be needed.
To apply this framework to a report or a wealth situation, it is useful to record assets, liabilities, the share of securities, deposits and insurance or pensions separately. The second check is to verify whether the figure is nominal or real; the third is to ask whether growth derives from new investments or from increases in value in the markets. These are exactly the distinctions the report uses to compare Switzerland, Western Europe and the global picture.
Before comparing two figures, it is also necessary to note the unit and scope: the report alternates between per-capita values, household data and global aggregates, as well as euros, francs and dollars. This note prevents placing the average figure per Swiss person and the total wealth of a region on the same footing.
This procedure does not turn the 9% estimate into a guarantee and does not eliminate the risks described by analysts. It serves to read gross, net and real figures using the same scale and to recognize how much the equity component can affect the results.
To link these indicators to earned income, use the calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

item.title: Swiss eggs: “misleading” to talk about small farms
item.description: The Swiss Commission for Fairness deems an advertisement by Suisse Garantie misleading: 65% of laying hens live on farms with more than 4000 animals.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The small-scale farming formula was judged misleading - 65% of laying hens live in farms with over 4,000 specimens - 80% live in facilities with more than 2,000 hens - The contested video dates back to February 2026
## Key facts - Decision → Swiss Commission for Fairness (SLK) - Advertising → Suisse Garantie - Contested video → February 2026 - Cited data → 65% over 4,000; 80% over 2,000 - Indicated natural size → about 30 hens - Dissemination of the decision → Werbemist platform
### The decision on advertising
The Swiss Commission for Fairness (SLK) has ruled that Suisse Garantie's advertising on Swiss eggs is misleading when it talks about small-scale farming. The complaint had been submitted by several animal protection organizations. The SLK is the self-regulatory body of the advertising industry.
The recommendation addressed to Suisse Garantie is not to use the contested claim in the future. The decision was made public by the animal protection platform Werbemist. The dispute concerns the use of the formula in advertising.
The case concerns a promotional video released in February 2026. In the footage, Suisse Garantie claimed that Swiss eggs came mainly from family-run farms, with 'small-scale farming, animal welfare-friendly barns and excellent care'. It is this combination of messages that has been contested.
Animal rights organizations cited data according to which 65% of laying hens in Switzerland live in farms with over 4,000 specimens and 80% in facilities with more than 2,000. The natural size of a group, indicated at about 30 hens, would thus be largely exceeded, according to their argument.
Critics added that the majority of laying hens live under intensive farming conditions. They also recalled the painful sternum fractures affecting numerous birds and the slaughter of the animals after about a year. The SLK's decision aligned with the contestation on the small-scale farming formula and recommended not to propose it again.
The reference to family management alone does not answer the question about the size of the farms. In the examined case, the complaint linked that positive description with data on the facilities housing laying hens. The SLK accepted this approach, recommending to refrain from the contested formula. For consumers, the central element of the measure thus remains the contrast between the promotional expression and the dimensions indicated by the complainants. ## Practical impact for consumers
### Reading beyond the advertising promise
For those living in Switzerland, the practical point described by the source is to understand what information a commercial promise conveys. The report does not quantify prices, available quantities or sales rules. The practical effect can therefore be understood without attributing to the decision consequences that are not indicated.
The first distinction concerns the management of the company and the size of the group. A family-run business is a description of its management; a small farm, on the other hand, concerns the number of animals. The video combined both ideas, while the appellants countered with numerical thresholds. The cautious reading is not to use one promise to automatically infer the other.
| Expression or data | Practical reading | | Family-run farms | Description present in the video | | Small farms | Formula challenged by the CSL | | More than 4000 animals | 65% of laying hens, according to the data cited by the appellants | | More than 2000 animals | 80% of laying hens, according to the same data | | Approximately 30 hens | Natural group size indicated by the animal-rights activists |
The second distinction concerns the size of the farms and animal welfare. The video associated small farms with animal-friendly barns and excellent care; the critics responded by pointing to intensive farming, breastbone fractures and slaughter after about a year. The source attributes these points to the critics: it does not present them as a separate measurement by the CSL. This boundary is also practical, because it makes it possible to understand the challenge without turning every element of the debate into an undifferentiated description of all farms.
The before-and-after comparison is limited but clear: before, the video presented Swiss origin, family management, small farms and positive conditions together; after the decision, Suisse Garantie was invited to refrain from using the contested wording in the future. Anyone planning a food budget can consult the costo della vita in Svizzera, but this case provides no egg prices and does not allow a saving to be estimated.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to verify the message
### A five-step verification
To use this decision when encountering an advertisement about Swiss eggs, it is advisable to follow a five-step verification. It is not a formal complaints procedure: it is a way to separate promotional wording from the data reported in the news article.
1. Identify the phrase. Check whether the message presents Swiss eggs as coming mainly from family-run farms and small-scale holdings. 2. Separate the claims. Swiss origin, family management, farm size and animal welfare are distinct elements of the message. 3. Compare the thresholds. Keep separate the figure of 65% of laying hens in farms with over 4000 specimens and that of 80% in facilities with more than 2000; the source does not add them together. 4. Preserve the attribution. The figures are data cited by the complainants, while the natural size of a group is given as approximately 30 hens by animal-rights activists. 5. Check the measure. The CSL recommended that Suisse Garantie refrain in future from using the disputed wording.
If the message reappears, the date of the video examined, febbraio 2026, helps distinguish the material cited in the news article from other content. The Werbemist platform made the decision public, but the source does not describe a procedure for consumers. For this reason, the process below remains a verification of the message, not an administrative procedure invented from the case.
The welfare findings also require precision. The majority of laying hens kept in intensive conditions, painful breastbone fractures and slaughter after about one year are elements reported by critics. They should therefore be presented as objections reported by the source, not as an undifferentiated conclusion about every farm.
The same applies to the percentages: the threshold of over 4000 specimens and that of more than 2000 describe different categories. The figure of 30 hens is not a new advertising threshold, but the natural size of a group indicated by animal-rights activists.
The source does not provide egg prices or a comparison in Swiss francs and euros. For a separate currency comparison, comparatore CHF/EUR is available. To link the verification to your personal budget, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Prisoners domiciled abroad: no LAMal obligation
item.description: After the Council of States' vote in June, the National Council rejected the amendment to LAMal with no votes in favor: the costs of detainees remain with the Cantons.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - No LAMal obligation for prisoners domiciled abroad - The National Council voted with no votes in favour - Around 2.000 people in prison without AOMS in 2021 - The costs remain the responsibility of the cantons
## Key facts - Location → Bern - National Council vote → no votes in favour - Outcome → consideration rejected - Previous vote → Council of States, June - Estimate → around 2.000 people without AOMS in 2021 - Statistics → FHE of the Federal Statistical Office (UST/BFS) - Law → amendment to LAMal - Current funding → cantonal taxes
In Bern, after the vote of the Council of States in June, the National Council rejected, with no votes in favour, consideration of the relevant amendment to the Health Insurance Act. The result rules out introducing an obligation for prisoners in Switzerland who are domiciled abroad to take out insurance with a health insurance fund.
The process stopped at the consideration stage: Parliament did not proceed to a detailed examination of the proposed amendment. A new federal obligation is therefore ruled out for the group concerned.
### The federal vote
The proposal sought to shift the healthcare costs of foreign prisoners from the public purse to health insurance funds. The Federal Council's bill had a stated objective: to ensure equal medical treatment during detention, as provided for by the Federal Constitution. To achieve this, the reform would have enrolled the persons concerned in health insurance and required them to pay the premium.
The framework described by the source is different. The healthcare costs of prisoners not domiciled in Switzerland are currently borne by the cantons and financed through cantonal taxes. The National Council's decision therefore maintains the existing framework for the group concerned. The legislative reference was LAMal/KVG; guida LAMal can be consulted for guidance on the topic.
### Figures and reasons for the rejection
The Deprivation of Liberty Statistics, identified by the acronym FHE, from the Federal Statistical Office (UST/BFS), estimated that in 2021 around 2.000 people were in prison without compulsory health insurance for medical care (AOMS). This figure is the statistical basis cited in the dossier.
Parliament opposed the transfer almost unanimously. According to the reasons given, it would have been inappropriate to shift the costs from the cantons to compulsory insurance, also because many of those concerned would have benefited from premium reductions. The reform would also have created a disproportionate administrative burden: as a rule, those concerned would have been enrolled in health insurance for only a few months. The matter was deemed to fall under cantonal jurisdiction. With the votes of the Council of States and the National Council, the dossier has been definitively buried. ## What changes, and what does not
The practical point of the rejection is the failure to transfer the costs. For the audience described by the source, funding remains in the channel already indicated: the Cantons bear the healthcare expenses of non-domiciled prisoners and cover them through cantonal taxes. On the other hand, the mechanism that would have required the individuals concerned to pay a health insurance premium is not created.
### Before, proposal, outcome
| Phase | Mechanism | |---|---| | Current situation | Healthcare costs borne by the Cantons and funded by cantonal taxes | | Proposed reform | Health insurance premium paid by the individuals concerned | | Parliamentary outcome | Transfer from the Cantons to compulsory insurance rejected |
The comparison also clarifies the scope of the decision. The proposal did not concern a general revision of premiums for those living in Switzerland, but a specific audience of detained individuals domiciled abroad. The source does not announce a new obligation for other insured persons nor a general amount to be applied to families. Therefore, the vote should not be read as a decision on the premiums of the general population. Its subject remains the funding of medical care during detention for the individuals indicated in the proposal.
For the administrations, the reported problem was the limited duration of the insurance relationship: those concerned would normally have been affiliated for only a few months. Parliament considered the administrative burden associated with such a short affiliation to be disproportionate. Added to this was the issue of premium reductions, which would have involved many of those concerned according to the reported reasoning.
The choice therefore has a precise effect on the institutional level: a new federal step is not created to shift the health bill towards compulsory insurance. The issue has remained associated with cantonal jurisdiction. For those looking at the cost of living, the consequence should not be broadened beyond the dossier: the source speaks of healthcare costs of non-domiciled prisoners and cantonal taxes, not a revision of direct federal tax. The expenditure framework can be explored in greater depth under cost of living in Switzerland, without confusing this decision with a general change in premiums.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to read the decision
The decision does not require turning a parliamentary news item into a new compliance obligation. For anyone who has to assess a case related to detention, the useful sequence is as follows:
1. Define the scope. The text concerns detainees in Switzerland who are domiciled abroad and the proposal concerning foreign detainees; it should not automatically be extended to all detainees. 2. Separate the data from the decision. Approximately 2.000 is an estimate referring to 2021 in the FHE of the UST/BFS, not the numerical result of the parliamentary vote. 3. Distinguish the current regime from the reform. For prisoners who are not domiciled in Switzerland, the source indicates cantonal financing through cantonal taxes; the premium paid by individuals was the proposed mechanism. 4. Check the status. The Council of States had rejected it in June; the National Council then refused to consider it, with no votes in favor. The dossier has been definitively shelved. 5. Keep the level of jurisdiction clear. Parliament considered the matter cantonal, so the decision does not trigger a federal procedure.
### What follows from the vote
Once these steps have been completed, there is no new federal compliance obligation to derive from the vote. The insurance obligation for the indicated group was not introduced, and the transfer of costs to health insurers was not approved. The correct interpretation is therefore institutional, not a request for immediate enrollment.
The same caution applies to the numbers. The FHE estimate from 2021 is the statistical data cited in the dossier; the reference to a few months instead describes the duration normally expected for the affiliation envisaged by the reform. These are two different elements: the first quantifies the people without compulsory health insurance, while the second supports Parliament's administrative objection.

item.title: Rising housing and mobility costs: spending on the rise in Switzerland
item.description: In August 2026, prices related to housing and mobility in Switzerland show a +2,4% increase, with an additional burden of 89 francs per month for families.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Housing and mobility: +2,4% in August 2026 - Households spend 89 francs more per month - In Italian-speaking Switzerland, annual inflation reaches 3% - Fuel: +17,9% in one year
## Key facts - Period → August 2026 - Scope → housing and mobility - Average price increase → 2,4% - CPI comparison → 0,8% - Italian-speaking Switzerland → 3% - Budget share → around 40% of daily consumption - Monthly expenditure → 89 francs more - Over one year → 1’066 francs more
In August 2026, prices related to housing and mobility in Switzerland increased by 2,4% compared with the same month of the previous year. The comparison with the national Consumer Price Index (CPI) of the Federal Statistical Office is clear: the CPI rose by 0,8%, meaning that the price increase in the two sectors is three times higher. In Italian-speaking Switzerland, the annual increase reaches 3%. In Ticino, the price increase for mobility and housing costs is the highest.
This figure is contained in Comparis’s MAb price index, published quarterly since March 2024 in collaboration with the KOF Swiss Economic Institute at ETH Zurich. For housing, the index considers, among other things, rents, energy and furnishings; for mobility, fuel, cars and public transport. According to Comparis, the two categories account on average for around 40% of the budget for the daily consumption of a Swiss household.
The impact in francs can be illustrated by a concrete example from the analysis: a family that a year ago spent 2’500 francs per month on rent, 1’000 on a car and 200 on public transport must now budget around 89 francs more per month. Over twelve months, the increase amounts to 1’066 francs for housing and mobility expenses alone.
### The car category weighs more than fuel alone
In August, fuel cost an average of 17,9% more than a year earlier. Diesel increased by 23,3% and petrol by 15,8%. Motor vehicle insurance rose by +7,4% year-on-year and by +18,9% over five years. Spare parts and accessories increased by 12,6%, while maintenance and repairs rose by 8,6%.
Purchase prices are moving in the opposite direction: new cars cost 0,8% less than a year ago, while used cars cost 1,5% less.
> «For motorists, it is not only the costs at the pump that are increasing. Insurance, spare parts and repairs are also having an ever-greater impact on household budgets. Due to the geopolitical situation in the Middle East, which remains uncertain, a significant improvement in the situation in the near future is unlikely», says Dirk Renkert, Comparis finance expert. ## Heating and spending profiles
### Heating divides spending
The energy component shows that the price increase does not affect all households in the same way. Energy for heating includes gas, heating oil, firewood and district heating; in Comparis' analysis, it is the second-highest increase.
| Item | Annual change | |---|---:| | Heating oil | +53,1% | | Energy for heating | +17,1% | | Firewood | +10,8% | | District heating | -0,4% | | Gas | -3% |
The differences between the items change how the budget is viewed: a home heated with heating oil follows different dynamics from one connected to gas or district heating. The energy source therefore affects the financial burden in very different ways. For tenants, however, the type of source used to heat the apartment is difficult to change in the short term. Renkert recommends reducing consumption and allowing sufficient room in the household budget when heating costs fluctuate sharply.
After energy for heating, among the most significant increases are other furniture, including bedroom and garden furniture, which rose by 3,5%, and furnishing accessories and non-fixed carpets, which increased by 3,1%. Not all items rose, however: small household appliances fell by 8,1%, other consumer goods for household use by 4,8%, large household appliances by 4,3%, motorized tools for home and garden by 3,6%, and electricity by 3%.
### Differences by age and income
The household profile changes the index result. Over the last twelve months, the largest increase in the housing and mobility sectors concerns couples over 65 without children: +2,5% year on year and +0,7% compared with May 2026. Single people over 65 are instead the least affected: the index stands at 114 points, with an annual increase of 2,2% and an increase of 0,6% compared with May.
Income also makes a difference. The middle-income bracket records an increase of 2,6% in one year and 0,6% compared with May; for the lowest income bracket, prices rose by 2,3% year on year and by 0,6% in the last quarter. To read these differences together with other household expenses, you can consult costo della vita in Svizzera, keeping heating, mobility and furniture separate.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## From data to budget control
### Five practical steps
To use the figures from the MAb index in the household budget, it is advisable to work by line items and like-for-like comparisons. The objective is to understand which housing and mobility expenses are changing, without conflating them.
1. Divide expenses into housing and mobility. In the first group, include rent, energy and furniture; in the second, fuel, cars and mezzi pubblici. These are the categories indicated by the index.
2. Compare the same month with a year earlier. As a reference, the analysis uses a family that spent 2’500 francs on rent, 1’000 on the car and 200 on public transport: the resulting change is approximately 89 francs per month, equal to 1’066 francs over a year.
3. For the car, separate fuel from motor vehicle insurance, spare parts and accessories, maintenance and repairs. Add the price of the car on a separate line, so that the review does not stop at fuel.
4. For heating, identify the energy source used in the apartment. If costs fluctuate significantly, Renkert’s recommendation is to reduce consumption and allow a sufficient margin in the household budget. For tenants, the source is practically unchangeable in the short term.
5. Repeat the check quarterly, following the MAb index, published quarterly since March 2024. Those living in Italian-speaking Switzerland can read their own trend alongside the annual figure of 3%, indicated by the analysis for this area.
This framework leads to clearer monitoring: rent remains separate from energy, the cost of the car remains separate from public transport and heating fluctuations are observed separately. When pressure on car costs emerges, regular comparison of motor vehicle insurance rates is the check suggested by Renkert; when heating costs fluctuate, the indicated priority is to leave room and reduce consumption.
To link budget monitoring to your monthly income, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Sharp increases for cars and housing, especially in Ticino
item.description: In August, housing and mobility costs rise by 2.4% in Switzerland. Ticino records the highest annual increase at 3%.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Mobility and housing: +2,4% in August year on year - Overall inflation: 0,8% - Ticino records the highest annual increase: 3% - Fuel 17,9% more expensive on average
## Key facts - Period → August; MAb index → 2,4% - Overall inflation → 0,8%; hardest-hit region → Ticino - Fuel → 17,9%; heating → 17,1% - Regional comparison → Ticino 3%; middle class → 2,6%
In August, housing and mobility costs rose by 2,4% compared with the same month last year, three times overall inflation, which stood at 0,8%. Ticino showed the sharpest growth. The figure contributes to understanding the cost of living in Switzerland, but the index specifically concerns housing and mobility.
The report comes from Comparis, an online comparison portal cited by Keystone-ATS. In collaboration with the KOF Institute, the business-cycle research center of the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich, Comparis calculates the mobility and housing price index, called MAb.
The scope remains the one described by the source: housing, automobiles, public transport and heating. It is therefore not an update on AVS/AHV, LPP/BVG, LAMal/KVG, VAT or direct federal tax, items that are not covered here.
To understand the effect on the household budget, the source offers an example. If a family spent 2500 francs a month last year on rent, 1000 on a car and 200 on public transport tickets, with a 2,4% increase, costs rose by around 89 francs a month. Over the entire year, the increase reached 1066 francs for housing and mobility. This is the kind of comparison that readers can explore further in costo della vita in Svizzera.
### The cost of owning a car
The financial burden is particularly severe for motorists. In August, fuel cost 17,9% more on average than a year earlier: diesel had become 23,3% more expensive and petrol 15,8%. Motor vehicle insurance cost 7,4% more; over five years, the increase reached 18,9%. Spare parts and accessories rose by 12,6%, while maintenance and repairs rose by 8,6%. New cars were 0,8% cheaper and used ones 1,5% cheaper.
> «For drivers, it is not only the costs at the pump that are increasing»
Dirk Renkert, Comparis' finance expert, quoted in a press release, emphasizes that insurance, spare parts and repairs weigh more heavily on household budgets. In his view, because of the still uncertain geopolitical situation in the Middle East, a significant improvement in the near future is unlikely. ## Heating divides households
### Energy sources with opposing trends
Heating energy prices rose overall by 17,1%. However, the aggregate figure masks opposing movements among the sources: heating oil rose in price by 53,1%, firewood by 10,8%; district heating, on the other hand, decreased by 0,4% and gas by 3,0%.
| Source | Annual change | |---|---:| | Heating oil | +53,1% | | Firewood | +10,8% | | District heating | -0,4% | | Gas | -3,0% |
The gap materially changes the weight of the bill in the household budget. The type of energy source used to heat a dwelling has a strong impact on the financial burden and, for tenants, can hardly be changed in the short term. For this reason, the source urges people to reduce consumption and allow for a sufficient margin when heating costs fluctuate significantly.
### The regional difference
The comparison by language region places Ticino in first place for annual price increases: the increase is 3% (3,0% in the reported figure). Compared with May 2026, the price level in the region rose by 0,7%.
At national level, returning to income brackets, the increase in the cost of living was more pronounced for the middle class. For this category, the MAb index rose by 2,6% year on year and by 0,6% compared with May. The twofold comparison, annual and monthly, shows two different perspectives: the first measures the distance from the same period of the previous year, while the second measures the movement compared with May 2026.
The regional difference concerns those who live in the Cantons, while the income bracket indicates that the same price increase does not weigh equally on all households. Public transport tickets are also included in the overall calculation; for this item, readers can consult mezzi pubblici.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Four checks to keep spending under control
### From the pump to the thermostat
Comparis points to a series of practical measures to reduce the impact of mobility and housing expenses. They do not require changing the scope of the index: they serve to review the items on which a family can act directly.
1. **Fuel.** Compare prices among different service stations and regions before choosing where to refuel.
2. Insurance. Periodically review long-term policies, seeking more affordable solutions suited to one's situation.
3. Heat loss. Reduce heat loss through proper ventilation, keeping shutters and curtains closed at night and leaving radiators unobstructed.
4. Heating. Optimize the system by lowering the temperature by even just one degree.
The sequence makes it possible to separate decisions about mobility from those concerning housing. Comparing fuel prices concerns car-related spending; reviewing policies addresses a recurring cost; the last two measures concern the home's energy consumption.
For tenants, the home's energy source remains difficult to modify in the short term. It therefore becomes more important to act on consumption and leave some room in the household budget in case of sharp fluctuations in heating costs.

item.title: Health insurers: cap on executives' salaries
item.description: The lower chamber approves the amendment to LVAMal: 157 votes in favor, 27 against, and 8 abstentions. The dossier now goes to the Council of States.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The lower house approves the bill with 157 votes - 27 against and 8 abstentions on the bill - The Federal Council proposed a cap equivalent to the seven ministers’ compensation - The dossier now goes to the Council of States
## Key facts - Subject → amendment of LVAMal - Proposed cap → compensation no higher than the highest class under the Federal Personnel Act - Transparency → names, salaries and employment rate of executives - Vote → 157 in favour, 27 against and 8 abstentions - Next step → Council of States
The lower house approved the amendment to LVAMal with 157 votes in favour, 27 against and 8 abstentions. The bill provides that health-insurance fund executives receive compensation no higher than that of the highest class established by the Federal Personnel Act.
The text amends LVAMal, identified in the source as the Federal Act on the Supervision of Social Health Insurance. The bill concerns basic health insurance, described in the source as social insurance paid through mandatory premiums. The proposal combines the remuneration limit with a transparency objective: publishing the names, salaries and employment rates of the various executives.
### The debate in the chamber
A minority had called for the matter not to be considered. Its arguments were a possible increase in bureaucracy and limited potential savings on healthcare costs. The Federal Council, on the other hand, supported a different benchmark: setting the maximum compensation of executives at that of the seven ministers.
Brigitte Crottaz (PS/VD), speaking on behalf of the majority of the Social Security and Health Committee, defended the bill, arguing that the remuneration of some executives reaches levels that are difficult to explain. According to the member of parliament, transparency should concern not only the amount, but also the identity and employment rate of executives.
Valérie Piller Carrard (FR) added that the salaries of executives at the main insurance groups also increased last year, while premiums continued to rise. Andri Silberschmidt (PLR/ZH) defended the minority and called the bill «homeopathic». In his view, the costs for insured persons attributable to salaries in basic coverage amount to 3 francs per person per year, less than an espresso in Zurich. The Radical Liberal also argued that most of executives’ salaries would be generated through supplementary benefits. ## Two benchmarks for the same cap
The point requiring the most attention in the parliamentary debate is the benchmark chosen for the cap. The lower house linked the maximum remuneration to the highest class under the Confederation's personnel law; the Federal Council, by contrast, had indicated that of the seven ministers. These are two different criteria, and the source does not provide an amount in francs for either of them. Nor does it indicate the individual salaries of the executives. Readers can therefore compare the political parameters, but cannot derive a new maximum salary expressed in francs from this dossier.
The figure cited in the chamber comes from Andri Silberschmidt's position and concerns the costs for insured persons that end up in salaries for basic coverage. His calculation is 3 francs per person per year, less than an espresso in Zurich. The minority uses it to argue that the potential for savings on healthcare expenses is limited and that most executive remuneration comes from supplementary insurance. The majority, by contrast, insists on levels that are difficult to explain and on the growth in salaries at the major insurance groups despite the increase in premiums.
For those observing the effect on the family budget, the figure can be read alongside costo della vita in Svizzera, but it must not be turned into a general estimate of premiums: the source reports only the calculation attributed to the minority representative.
### Transparency beyond the figure
The bill links oversight of remuneration to the publication of three elements: name, salaries and employment rate of the various executives. The discussion, therefore, concerns not only the maximum threshold, but also the possibility of associating each remuneration with the position and employment level indicated in the bill. To follow the issue of health insurers, this distinction avoids confusing the pay cap with the transparency required.
### The boundary with supplementary insurance
Mattea Meyer (PS/ZH) had proposed banning “mixed funds,” legal structures in which both basic-insurance policyholders and supplementary-insurance policyholders are handled, in order to prevent a transfer of costs. The amendment was rejected by 129 votes to 63. The proposal by Basel-based Socialist Samira Marti to extend certain provisions to supplementary insurance was rejected in turn by 127 votes to 65. The source therefore records two extensions not accepted by the lower house.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to follow the dossier
To follow the dossier without conflating decisions already made, alternatives discussed, and proposals rejected, the reading can be organized into four checks. These are the points that emerge from the debate addressed by the lower chamber.
### Four checks to keep separate
1. **Subject matter.** Read each update, checking that it concerns the amendment to LVAMal and the compensation of health-insurance executives. These are the elements at the center of the adopted text.
2. Parameter. Look for the reference to the highest class under the Federal Personnel Act. If the reference to the seven ministers appears, it instead concerns the approach proposed by the Federal Council.
3. Transparency. Check whether the three indicated elements remain in the bill: name, salaries, and employment rate of the executives. This check must be made separately from the pay limit.
4. Scope. Keep separate the bill on basic coverage, the proposal on «mixed funds» rejected by 129 votes to 63, and the extension to supplementary insurance rejected by 127 votes to 65.
### The next step
The institutional sequence indicated by the source is clear: after the lower chamber's decision, the Council of States will have to rule on the dossier. This is the next check to make before considering the rule finalized. The available text does not close the process and does not allow either the pay threshold or the publication of the data to be presented as already operative.
When the next vote takes place, the first information to isolate will be the solution chosen for the limit; the second will concern transparency; the third will be the treatment of supplementary insurance. This sequence avoids attributing to the approved amendment amendments that have already been rejected.
To follow the issue, the guide to health insurers can accompany monitoring without confusing basic coverage with supplementary insurance. For a personal comparison of income, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Lindt & Sprüngli cuts growth estimates for 2026
item.description: Lindt e Sprüngli lowers its 2026 organic revenue growth forecast to between 0 and 2% due to heat and prices.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Organic growth 2026: between 0 and 2%. - Previous estimate: between 4 and 6%. - Summer heat and prices weigh on orders in Europe. - 2026 EBIT margin confirmed: 20-40 basis points.
## Key facts - Company → Lindt&Sprüngli - Location → Kilchberg - New 2026 estimate → organic revenue growth between 0 and 2% - Previous estimate → organic revenue growth between 4 and 6% - 2026 EBIT target → improvement of 20-40 basis points - Next 2027 forecast → publication in the first quarter - Targets from 2028 → annual organic revenue growth between 6 and 8%
### The revision announced in Kilchberg
Lindt&Sprüngli has significantly revised down its forecast for organic revenue growth in 2026. In a statement released Tuesday, the chocolate maker now indicates a range between 0 and 2%, whereas the previous expectation was set between 4 and 6%.
The group attributes the correction to two factors: strong consumer price sensitivity and the extreme summer heatwave. In Europe, CEO Adalbert Lechner explained, the price increases deemed necessary and cautious consumer sentiment resulted in order volumes below expectations.
The weakness mainly affected seasonal business in Germany, Switzerland and Austria. The geographical picture is not uniform, however: in North America and Asia Lindt&Sprüngli recorded robust growth. The statement therefore presents differing dynamics across the group’s regions.
On the cost front, Lindt&Sprüngli expects pressure to gradually normalize in the coming months, following the decline in cocoa prices from historic highs.
For 2026, the target of improving the EBIT margin by 20-40 basis points compared with the previous year remains confirmed. For 2027, the group expects a return to volume growth, supported by an adapted pricing strategy, greater brand investment, falling cocoa prices and rigorous cost management.
The financial forecasts for 2027 will be published in the first quarter. The medium-term targets from 2028 are also confirmed: annual organic revenue growth of 6-8% and an annual improvement in the EBIT margin of 20-40 basis points. The message thus separates three horizons: the reduced estimate for 2026, the expected return to volume growth in 2027 and the medium-term targets from 2028. ## The comparison for the Swiss audience
### Three ranges not to be confused
The practical figure to isolate is the gap between the growth ranges, not just their final value. 2% is the upper limit of the new estimate for organic revenue in 2026. 6% is both the upper limit of the previous 4-6% range and the lower limit of the 6-8% target expected from 2028. 8% instead represents the ceiling of the annual organic growth indicated for the medium term.
| Horizon | Indicator | Value | | --- | --- | --- | | 2026 | Organic revenue growth | 0-2% | | Previous estimate | Organic revenue growth | 4-6% | | 2027 | Volumes | Return to growth | | From 2028 | Annual organic revenue growth | 6-8% |
The comparison shows a clear trajectory: 2026 is revised downward, while 2027 is associated with a recovery in volumes. The target from 2028 returns to a broader range, but remains a medium-term target and not an additional forecast for 2026.
### The Swiss part of the picture
Switzerland is cited together with Germany and Austria among the countries where weakness particularly affected seasonal activity. For the group, the price increases considered necessary and the cautious consumer climate were accompanied by orders below expectations in Europe. The source does not quantify the separate effect of the heat, nor does it indicate a specific price for consumers.
The second element to observe is the cost side. The decline in cocoa from historic highs supports the expectation of a gradual normalization of pressure, while the pricing strategy should be adapted for 2027. For those living in Switzerland, the comparison with their own budget can start from costo della vita in Svizzera, without turning the company forecast into an individual estimate of spending.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow the next updates
The source already indicates a useful schedule for monitoring developments, but not a specific date. The reader can therefore follow the matter with a simple procedure and separate company data from personal assessments.
### A three-step procedure
1. Note the range expected for 2026 and keep it alongside the previous estimate. The comparison should remain focused on organic revenue growth, without confusing it with volumes or the EBIT margin.
2. Read separately the three signals indicated by the group: order volumes in Europe, pricing strategy and cost pressure. These are different areas, linked respectively to demand, commercial policy and the performance of cocoa.
3. Mark the first quarter as the next checkpoint. This is the period indicated for the publication of financial forecasts relating to 2027. When they become available, the comparison should focus on the return to volume growth and on the objectives stated for the subsequent time horizon.
For a personal reading, it is advisable to keep the company's data separate from one's own situation. The communication refers to price sensitivity, cautious consumption and orders below expectations, but does not translate these elements into a figure valid for every consumer. Anyone who wants to verify their starting point can use the busta paga svizzera as a reference.
