item.description: Vaud approves a 12% reduction in cantonal income and substance taxes. There is talk of 272 million less from next January 1.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Vaud has voted in favor of a 12% tax reduction - 272 million less in revenue are expected - The Government has three months for the 2027 budget - The unions say they are ready to mobilize
## Key facts - Decision: yes to the initiative - Taxes: cantonal income and wealth taxes - Revenue: 272 million less - Deadline: next 1 January - State Council: two weeks for proposals - Assembly: 8 October
## The vote opens the budget dossier The Canton of Vaud has voted in favor of the initiative calling for a 12% reduction in cantonal taxes on the income and wealth of individuals. The figure indicated for the lower revenue is 272 million. The lost revenue is indicated as starting next 1 January, but the source does not yet indicate how the impact will be distributed among the different sectors.
For those living in the Canton, the vote therefore shifts the discussion from taxation to the sustainability of public services. The initiative’s proponents have promised that services will not be changed. Public services in Vaud are nevertheless on alert: the Government has three months to prepare the 2027 budget, and the question dominating the debate is where to make savings.
### The request to be consulted Jean-Luc Andrey, president of the Vaud association of medico-psycho-social institutions, recalled that during the 2025-2026 period, the institutions were presented with a fait accompli on the very day the budget was presented. He asked that the institutions be consulted, whatever decision affects them.
> “In 2025-2026, we were presented with a fait accompli on the very day the budget was presented. We do not want this to happen again: we are asking to be consulted, whatever decision is made regarding our institutions.”
The State Council has given itself two weeks to present its proposals to Parliament. In the meantime, the municipalities are watching the dossier because they are on the front line in managing services for citizens. Chantal Weidmann-Yenny, PLR president of the Association of Vaud Municipalities, identified as a risk the possibility that the municipalities would have to make up the revenue shortfall. She called for joint work with the Canton on infrastructure regulation and the issue of housing.
The unions have already announced possible mobilization if cuts are introduced. Catherine Friedli, SSP Vaud union secretary, said that there are already insufficient resources to guarantee the quality of public services and staff working conditions. The public service staff assembly is scheduled for 8 October, during the electoral period preceding the renewal of Parliament and Government scheduled for next February. ## The reduction is not the same as the entire tax To understand the effect on the household budget, it is necessary to separate the levels of the Swiss tax system. The system comprises direct federal tax, cantonal taxes and municipal taxes; the Cantons have their own law and multiplier, while municipalities apply a multiplier to the cantonal tax. The initiative approved in Vaud concerns the cantonal component of income and wealth tax for individuals. Thus, by its subject matter, it is not an intervention concerning direct federal tax or VAT.
The same distinction avoids confusing the vote with other items that affect personal finances. The reduction does not concern AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG, which are social security, nor LAMal/KVG, which is compulsory health insurance with per-capita premiums. It is not a measure concerning the minimum wage. The cost of living in Switzerland may change the concrete weight of a tax decision for a family, but the source does not provide an individual calculation or a new overall rate. The 12% therefore does not correspond to 12% of the entire personal tax burden.
### Three scenarios to follow The first scenario is the one promised by the promoters: services remain unchanged even after the cut. In this case, practical verification comes through the 2027 budget and the Government's proposals. The source does not yet list the sectors concerned or indicate a savings plan.
The second scenario is the one feared by the municipalities. If the revenue shortfall were to fall on them, the discussion would shift to the local management of services, infrastructure and housing. This is a concern expressed by the Union of Vaud Municipalities, not a decision already taken.
The third scenario is the trade-union one. If the savings entailed cuts, SSP Vaud announces mobilization and puts service quality and working conditions at the center. The staff assembly thus becomes an event to monitor, alongside the renewal of Parliament and Government next February.
| Scenario | What the source indicates | What to verify | |---|---|---| | Promoters' promise | Services without changes | 2027 budget | | Municipalities' concern | Possible deficit coverage | Canton's proposals | | Trade-union position | Mobilization in the event of cuts | Service conditions |
To focus on the personal budget, it is advisable to compare the tax component with other expenses, without calling something related to premiums or pension provision a tax reduction. The costo della vita in Svizzera helps put this picture into perspective. The dichiarazione delle imposte remains the reference for one's own tax situation, but it does not replace the decisions that the Canton still has to present.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## How to follow the decision The source leaves two elements open for anyone who has to estimate the concrete effect: the measure has been approved, but the State Council still has to present its proposals and the Government has to prepare the 2027 budget. For now, therefore, the useful procedure is a sequence of checks on public decisions, not a simulation based solely on 12%.
### Four practical steps 1. Mark the next 1° gennaio as the reference date for the announced lower revenue. The source provides only the overall figure of 272 million less, not a personal amount. 2. Wait for the proposals of the State Council, which has given itself two weeks to submit them to Parliament. This is the first institutional step indicated after the vote. 3. Follow the 2027 budget over the three months assigned to the Government. The point to verify is whether and how public services will be affected, given that the proponents have promised not to change their provision. 4. For those who work in public service or use municipal services, observe the discussion between the Canton, municipalities and unions. The staff assembly is scheduled for 8 ottobre; the renewal of Parliament and Government is expected next febbraio.
### How to avoid hasty interpretations It is not enough to multiply a personal figure by 12%. The source does not specify the remaining rates, the methods of application, any municipal indications, or how the lower revenue will be absorbed into public accounts. For this reason, the check must be carried out on two levels: on the one hand, the effect on one's own cantonal taxation; on the other, the budget choices that may affect services.
For the individual part, one can organize one's situation in dichiarazione delle imposte, distinguishing the cantonal component from the other tax items. This step does not yet make it possible to know a definitive saving, because the source does not publish a calculation by income or assets.
Political communication will also have an operational role: the proponents' promises, the State Council's proposals, Parliament's decisions, and the unions' response are different steps. Confusing them leads to presenting as already decided what remains to be defined, particularly with regard to municipalities and services.
The reader can therefore update their overview when the budget documents arrive and compare the items without conflating taxes, social security and insurance premiums. To estimate the effect on the personal budget, use calcolatore stipendio e imposte.

item.title: UBS under pressure: 90% capital for foreign branches
item.description: Council of States calls for 90% capital for UBS's foreign subsidiaries. The bank contests the measure, rekindling speculation about a merger with Morgan Stanley and other institutions.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Council of States calls for 90% capital for foreign subsidiaries. - UBS challenges the capital measure. - Blick cites at least eight institutions, with Morgan Stanley among the names. - Relocating the headquarters could affect tax revenues.
## Key facts - Decision → 90% core capital for UBS's foreign subsidiaries - Institution → Council of States - UBS's reaction → political outcome described as not a compromise - Potential counterparts → at least eight globally active financial institutions - Name cited → Morgan Stanley - Analyst → Rudolf Minsch, chief economist at Economiesuisse - Second expert → Aymo Brunetti, professor at the University of Bern - Tax effect → tax revenues if the headquarters are relocated
### The decision and assumptions about the future
ZURICH - The battle over the new rules for UBS is entering a new phase following the Council of States' request: the large Swiss bank should support its foreign subsidiaries with core capital amounting to 90%. UBS challenges the measure.
> UBS described the political outcome as «not a compromise».
According to an investigation by Blick, the upper chamber's decision has reignited speculation about a possible merger. At least eight globally active financial institutions are said to have expressed openness to talks with UBS's management. Among the names cited is Morgan Stanley, a US institution.
The discussion stems from two distinct but related elements in the debate: the capital requirement for foreign operations and possible talks with other global groups. The source thus describes the merger as a possibility reignited by the political decision.
Rudolf Minsch, chief economist at Economiesuisse, argues that UBS would not give up its corporate banking business in Switzerland. Any downsizing, however, could create difficulties, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises, particularly with regard to larger financing needs. Companies could therefore be forced to seek financing elsewhere, including abroad.
Aymo Brunetti, a professor at the University of Bern, takes a more reassuring view. In his opinion, a possible merger or relocation of the headquarters would be unlikely to have immediate consequences for private and corporate clients. UBS would continue to have an interest in keeping its private and corporate banking activities in Switzerland because they are profitable. The most visible effects could concern tax revenues if the headquarters were relocated.
Brunetti also considers both a merger and a relocation of the headquarters unlikely at present. Swiss identity would remain important, especially in wealth management; becoming a US bank could make UBS less attractive to some international clients, particularly in Asia. The new capital requirement could ultimately make expansion in the United States more difficult, one of the reasons for UBS's strong opposition, according to the economist. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the practical point is not choosing a future partner for UBS, but distinguishing which activities would be affected in the different scenarios described by the experts. The source compares corporate lending, customer services and tax domicile: three connected but not equivalent areas.
### Four scenarios to keep separate
The first concerns corporate banking. If the bank were to scale back its operations in Switzerland, according to Rudolf Minsch, small and medium-sized enterprises would be the most exposed when seeking large amounts of financing. In this scenario, the issue is not presented as a general difficulty for every customer, but as the risk of having to seek credit elsewhere, including outside the country. For a company, the concrete question is therefore how dependent it is on UBS for its larger transactions.
The second scenario is a merger or relocation of the headquarters. Aymo Brunetti considers immediate consequences for private and corporate customers difficult, because UBS would have an interest in retaining private and corporate banking in Switzerland, which are profitable activities. This reduces the idea of an automatic effect on banking relationships, without eliminating the issue of the headquarters.
| Scenario | Effect indicated in the source | |---|---| | Scaling back | Possible difficulties for small and medium-sized enterprises, especially with larger financing | | Merger or relocation | Difficult immediate consequences for private and corporate customers | | Relocation of the headquarters | Possible effects on tax revenues | | Possible US bank | Potentially lower appeal for some customers in Asia | | New requirement | Possible expansion in the United States becoming more difficult |
For those who manage conti bancari in Svizzera, this distinction helps avoid confusing service continuity with broader economic consequences. The third and fourth scenarios in fact concern the taxation of the headquarters, the international appeal of Swiss identity and UBS's ability to expand in the United States. The source does not present them as a single outcome, but associates them with the different hypotheses. The decisive variable therefore remains the form that any change might take, not merely the fact that names of possible partners are circulating.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. An operational reading of the matter starts with a distinction: the tightening of capital is a political decision requested by the upper house, while the merger remains a possibility linked to the names mentioned by Blick. The verification must be updated without turning scenarios into established facts.
### Four steps to follow developments
1. Separate the formal fact from the market rumor. In one’s review, keep distinct the request concerning the core capital of foreign branches and the openness to talks reported by the investigation. Morgan Stanley should therefore be considered among the possible interlocutors mentioned, not as an announced merger.
2. Identify the area concerned. For a private client, the reference is to private banking activities; for a company, to corporate banking and more substantial financing. This distinction avoids automatically extending the effects discussed by economists to every service.
3. Assess the need for credit. A small or medium-sized company can assess whether any downsizing would make it necessary to seek financing elsewhere, including abroad. This is the scenario indicated by Minsch, not an undifferentiated forecast for all companies.
4. Keep services and headquarters separate. If the interest is fiscal, the issue concerns the possible relocation of the head office and tax revenues; if it concerns the banking relationship, Brunetti’s assessment is linked to the continued presence in Switzerland of private and corporate activities. To follow the former aspect, one can consult dichiarazione delle imposte, without confusing the two areas.
The final check consists of comparing each new development with the positions of UBS, Minsch and Brunetti. As long as the source speaks of possibilities, the reader can use these four filters to understand whether a news item concerns capital, credit, clients or the tax headquarters. This method avoids immediately attributing to private clients an effect that Brunetti places mainly at the level of the headquarters and tax revenues.

131.3 million francs for future reserve power plants were approved by the National Council in Berne by 118 votes to 74. The matter now goes to the Council of States.
Of the credit, 100 million are intended for planning and preparatory activities for the reserve power plants; the remaining 31.3 million will finance the Monthey (VS) plant, a transitional solution until 2030.

Two motions by Jacques Nicolet (UDC/VD) and Pierre-André Page (UDC/FR) were also approved. item.description: SNL forecasts losses of between 350'000 and 400'000 francs following the cantonal decision to no longer commission the Locarno-Magadino service
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - SNL begins the reorganization following the cantonal decision - Expected losses: between 350'000 and 400'000 francs - An «alternative contract» has been proposed to staff - Signing remains possible even after an initial refusal
## Key facts - Decision → Canton Ticino no longer commissions the service - Route → Locarno-Magadino - Expected losses → between 350'000 and 400'000 francs - Measures → reorganization and cost containment - Staff → alternative contract and redundancies reduced to a minimum - Developments → operational and commercial scenarios in the coming weeks
Società Navigazione del Lago di Lugano (SNL) has begun a reorganization following the decision by Canton Ticino to no longer commission the navigation service on the Locarno-Magadino route and not to cover any potential deficits. The company maintains that the decision by the Council of State will result in expected losses of between 350'000 and 400'000 francs.
### The reorganization and the alternative contract
According to SNL, the cantonal decision made cost containment necessary. The company says it has managed, «at least at this stage», to limit the consequences for staff: measures that are «less burdensome for staff» have been identified, and redundancies have been reduced to a minimum. The people involved were offered an «alternative contract». The possibility of signing it remains open even for those who had initially chosen not to accept it.
The assessment of the decision remains critical. SNL recalls that it took on the service on Lake Maggiore at the request of the Ticinese and federal authorities, providing public transport services over the years. In its view, the withdrawal of cantonal support unilaterally altered the economic conditions on which the service had been structured.
The matter thus affects the company's operations and the continuity of the service. The stated objective is to maintain an adequate level of service without excessively increasing ticket prices. SNL emphasizes that fares had been kept down because the services had been conceived as public transport and not as a simple commercial tourist offering.
> «We chose to do everything within our power to protect jobs and, at the same time, continue to guarantee a service to the region», says director Simone Bianchi.
In the coming weeks, SNL will continue to assess various operational and commercial scenarios. The statement thus leaves the way open both regarding staff and the service on Lake Maggiore. ### Before and after: where the economic risk shifts
The difference between the previous situation and the one described by SNL concerns how the navigation service is supported. Previously, the company says it had taken on the service on Lake Maggiore at the request of the Ticino and federal authorities; the trips were conceived as public transport and fares had been kept down. After the decision by Canton Ticino, the commission on the Locarno-Magadino route is discontinued and, according to the announcement, so is coverage of any deficits.
The economic figure makes the change in arrangement concrete: SNL expects losses of between 350'000 and 400'000 francs and is responding with a reorganization and cost containment. For staff, this means that the announced measure is linked to the sustainability of the service offering. The company says it chose less onerous solutions and minimized layoffs.
The alternative contract should therefore be viewed as the transition point between the political decision and the organization of work. The communication does not state the salary, working hours, duration or other conditions of the proposal: the announcement does not make it possible to determine an individual impact on income. The only explicit operational detail is that signing remains possible even for those who initially rejected it.
For users, there are two consequences to observe. On the one hand, there is the objective of maintaining an adequate level of service; on the other, there is the intention not to increase ticket prices excessively. The company does not indicate a new fare or a definitive operational solution. SNL instead speaks of various options to be assessed in the coming weeks.
Simone Bianchi's reading focuses on the transfer of risk: according to the director, the political decision places entirely on the company an economic risk previously linked to a public service commissioned by the Canton. For the region, the debate therefore concerns not only the company's accounts, but also what level of service can be maintained without turning the trips into a simple commercial tourist offering.

1. Read the proposal received. The certain reference is the 'alternative contract' intended for the people involved. The evaluation must start from the document actually proposed; salary, hours, and duration should only be considered if reported there.

item.description: The German antitrust authority has authorized Edeka to acquire 178 of Tegut’s 202 stores; 24 stores remain to be divested, along with 41 Teo locations, the Herzberger bakery, and a logistics center.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Edeka will take over 178 of the 202 Tegut stores - 24 stores remain to be assigned to other buyers - The package includes 41 Teo automated stores - The Fulda headquarters will close at the end of March 2027
## Key facts - Transaction approved → Edeka takes over 178 stores - Initial plan → 202 Tegut stores - Excluded stores → 24 - Included operations → 41 Teo stores, Herzberger bakery and logistics center - Regional markets examined → 34 - Ownership → Migros Zurich since 2013 - Tegut employees → approximately 7'400 - Headquarters closure → end of March 2027
## The German decision reshapes Migros's exit
ZURICH - Migros will have to find new buyers for 24 Tegut supermarkets in Germany. The German antitrust office has authorized Edeka to take over 178 of the 202 stores initially planned. The 24 excluded stores remain outside the transaction for competition-related reasons.
The approved package also includes 41 Teo automated stores, the Herzberger bakery and a logistics center. The sale therefore does not concern only the traditional supermarket network: these elements are part of the scope Edeka may take over.
Other buyers will be sought for the remaining stores, a spokesperson for the Migros Zurich cooperative explained to the AWP news agency. Migros welcomed the green light and says that its exit from the German food retail market is proceeding according to plan.
### Why the transaction was reduced
The German antitrust authority had been examining the transactions since March. According to the authority, the acquisition originally envisaged would have significantly hindered competition in 34 regional markets in Hesse, Thuringia, northern Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg. In nine of these markets, Edeka would also have established or strengthened a dominant position.
The assessment takes place in a highly concentrated German retail market. In 2025, Edeka, Rewe, the Schwarz Group, owner of Lidl and Kaufland, and Aldi accounted for more than 90% of total sales. Edeka was the largest operator, with a share of approximately 30%.
Tegut has belonged to Migros Zurich since 2013 and employs approximately 7'400 people. The closure of the Fulda headquarters is planned for the end of March 2027. Operations that are not transferred to a buyer will be liquidated as part of reconciliation-of-interests agreements and social plans.
In mid-March, Migros Zurich had announced its departure from the German market after 14 years, indicating an estimated maximum loss of 600 million euros. Approval of the Edeka transaction defines part of the exit, while the process for the 24 excluded stores remains to be completed. ## The before-and-after comparison
The practical effect of the decision is the separation of the original project. Edeka no longer acquires the entire scope initially planned: the approval concerns 178 supermarkets, while 24 must be assigned to other buyers. For the Swiss reader, this is the point to follow in subsequent updates, because the sale does not yet have a single outcome.
| Item | Initial plan | Authorized outcome | |---|---|---| | Tegut supermarkets | 202 for Edeka | 178 to Edeka; 24 to be placed | | Included network and activities | Planned transaction | 41 Teo, Herzberger bakery, logistics center | | Competition | Acquisition under review | Exclusions in 34 regional markets |
### What the decision actually measures
The table distinguishes the number of stores from the content of the package. The 41 Teo, the bakery and the logistics center remain within the approved scope; for this reason, the decision cannot be read solely as a reduction in the count of supermarkets. The source does not indicate whether the other buyers have already been identified or when the divestitures of the 24 stores will be completed.
The reference to the 34 markets and the nine cases in which a dominant position would have been created or strengthened explains why the authority separated part of the transaction. The issue examined is regional and competitive. The source, however, does not provide data on prices, consumers or purchasing conditions in Switzerland.
For Migros Zurigo, the corporate fact remains the exit from the German market and the maximum estimated loss. The text does not quantify effects on Swiss stores, wages or taxes; it therefore does not allow the decision to be turned into a forecast for these items. The approximately 7'400 employees also refer to Tegut as a whole: the source does not specify how many are connected to the 24 stores or the headquarters in Fulda.

## In brief - USAV: new biosecurity requirements for pig farms - Rules for professional and hobby operations - ASF compliance: facilitations in animal movements - Level 1 now, level 2 in the event of an epizootic outbreak
## Key facts - Authority: Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (USAV) - Location: Bern - Risk: African swine fever (ASF) - Scope: all pig farms - Current level: level 1 - In the event of an epizootic outbreak: level 2 - Measures indicated: access, hygiene and up-to-date documentation
### New requirements for farms
BERN - The Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (USAV) has defined new biosecurity requirements for pig farms. The objective indicated by the office is to protect animals from African swine fever, ASF.
The new development concerns so-called ASF compliance. Pig farms that meet the requirements may benefit from facilitations in animal movements if an epidemic occurs. The communication does not limit the scope to professional facilities: the rules apply to all pig farms, from professional breeding and fattening operations to hobby operations.
The requirements were developed in collaboration with companies in the sector, USAV announced. The collaboration therefore concerns the definition of the conditions for ASF compliance, while the communication attributes the definition of the new requirements to the federal office.
### What level 1 includes
The measures required include, first and foremost, the systematic prevention of any contact between domestic pigs and wild boars. This is followed by clearly defined access controls and hygiene measures at the entrance to the stables.
Biosecurity also includes documentation. USAV specifies complete and up-to-date documentation, including the visitor register, treatment log and daily recording of deaths and abortions.
The requirements now published concern level 1, intended for periods of calm, such as the current one. If an epizootic outbreak were to occur, the level would move to level 2, with additional measures adopted. The communication thus distinguishes between the procedures envisaged during the ordinary phase and those that would come into force during a health emergency. ## What changes at the operational level
The distinction between level 1 and level 2 helps read the measure as a graduated system. At level 1, which applies during periods of calm, biosecurity is based on the requirements published by USAV. In the event of an epizootic disease outbreak, the system instead moves to level 2, which entails adopting additional measures. The source specifies the change in level, but does not list the supplementary measures.
For a farm, PSA compliance does not consist of a single check. It is a set of interconnected practices and records. The separation of domestic pigs and wild boar concerns contact prevention; access control concerns who enters; hygiene concerns entry into the barns; records make the activities and events indicated by USAV documentable.
| Area | What the requirements require | |---|---| | Contacts | Systematic prevention of contact between domestic pigs and wild boar | | Access | Clearly defined controls | | Entry into the barns | Hygiene measures | | Documentation | Visitor log, treatment log, deaths and abortions recorded every day |
The comparison between compliant and non-compliant management becomes particularly evident in the event of an epidemic. Facilitations in animal movements are in fact linked to farms that meet the requirements. The rule thus creates a direct link between the work carried out during level 1 and the possibility of benefiting from facilitations when the health situation changes.
Applying the measure to all pig farms broadens its scope: both professional breeding and fattening operations and hobby farms are included. For those who also use the site's service tools, costo della vita in Svizzera and aziende che assumono are available.

To translate the USAV requirements into an operational check, a pig farm can proceed by following the order of the elements indicated in the communication. This sequence helps verify that none of the areas listed by the office is overlooked.
### A five-step checklist
1. Identify the activity. The verification concerns all pig farms, including professional breeding and fattening farms and hobby farms.
2. Check contacts. It is necessary to examine the systematic prevention of any contact between domestic pigs and wild boar, which represents the first requirement indicated by the USAV.
3. Define access and hygiene. Access controls must be clearly defined, and the required hygiene measures must be provided at the entrance to the barns.
4. Update the documentation. The visitor register and the treatment log are part of the documentation that must be kept complete and up to date. Deaths and abortions must be recorded daily.
5. Distinguish the levels. During the period of calm, level 1 applies. If an epizootic disease occurs, the situation moves to level 2, which entails additional measures.
The documentation aspect requires continuous attention: the USAV indicates not only the presence of the registers, but also that the documentation be complete and up to date. In addition, daily recording is indicated for deaths and abortions. Internal verification must therefore consider both physical and hygiene measures and the quality of the information retained.
This sequence does not introduce any additional data beyond the USAV communication: it organizes the published requirements in a practical form and clarifies the transition from level 1 to level 2. For the next check of the site's national tools, consult calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Reserve power plants: the National Council approves 131,3 million
item.description: The National Council has allocated 131,3 million francs for the planning and transitional solution of Monthey until 2030.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - National Council approves 131,3 million for reserve power plants - 100 million fund planning and preliminary activities - 31,3 million go to Monthey's transitional solution - The credit now goes to the Council of States
## Key facts - Decision → National Council - Vote → 118 votes to 74 - Amount → 131,3 million francs - Preparations → 100 million - Monthey (VS) → 31,3 million - Transitional solution → until 2030 - ElCom recommendation → at least 500 MW from 2030 - Next step → Council of States
### The vote and the project's dual-track approach
The National Council today approved, by 118 votes to 74, a credit of 131,3 million francs for future reserve power plants. The decision concerns the initial phase of the project and a solution already identified to support the system until 2030.
One hundred million francs will be allocated to planning and preliminary activities. The other 31,3 million will be used to finance the Monthey (VS) reserve power plant, which will serve as a transitional solution until 2030.
> “An electricity reserve is absolutely indispensable,” said Nicolas Kolly (UDC/FR) on behalf of the committee.
The rationale given in the chamber concerns the risk of a shortage also affecting neighboring countries. In such a situation, according to Kolly, Switzerland might not be able to count on sufficient imports. A severe shortage, he added, could cause economic damage amounting to billions of francs and consequences for security, society and the environment.
The Federal Electricity Commission, ElCom, recommends a permanent reserve capacity of at least 500 MW from 2030, in addition to the hydropower reserve. Building the infrastructure takes several years: for this reason, the text links the need for preparations to the early launch of planning.
The Federal Council had also requested 2,18 billion francs to build four new reserve power plants. The National Council's competent committee separated that part from the credit just approved. The credit of more than 2 billion will be discussed only next year, when ElCom publishes its periodic report on the security of electricity supply. The 131,3 million credit now goes to the Council of States. ### Three keys to understanding the effects
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the practical point is not only the amount approved, but the status of the dossier. The National Council approved funding for planning, preliminary activities and a transitional solution; the request to build the four new plants remains separate. A headline that automatically added 131,3 million and 2,18 billion would conflate two different phases.
The first key is the external risk described by the commission. If a shortage also affected neighboring countries, available imports might not be sufficient. The national reserve is therefore presented as a response to the risk of insufficient supplies. The damage envisaged is not solely economic: Kolly refers to billions of francs and consequences for security, society and the environment. These are the effects indicated by the source, not a prediction concerning a single family or company.
The second key is time. The infrastructure requires several years, and the Monthey solution runs until 2030. For the same horizon, ElCom indicates permanent capacity of at least 500 MW, additional to the hydroelectric reserve. For the reader, the difference between transitional and permanent helps explain why the funding for preparations is being examined before the decision on the broader project.
The third key is parliamentary. Consideration of the credit exceeding 2 billion is postponed until next year and linked to the publication of ElCom's periodic report on security of supply. Until that step, the source does not describe a definitive decision on the four plants.
The text does not indicate a new tariff or an obligation for individual residents. For those who also follow costo della vita in Svizzera, this distinction prevents attributing to the credit an effect that the source does not quantify. Here, the operational fact is the sequence of decisions on the electricity reserve: the risk of a shortage, advance planning and the subsequent parliamentary examination.

The source makes it possible to follow the dossier through a simple, entirely institutional procedure. The first step is to note the status of the decision: the credit has been approved by the National Council, and the next review falls to the Council of States. The second step is to separate the two financial tracks. When reading an update, it is necessary to check whether it concerns the credit already voted for planning, preliminary activities and Monthey, or the request, still to be discussed, for four new power plants. This distinction prevents the 2.18 billion from being presented as expenditure that has already been approved.
The third step is to establish two time references without turning them into dates that the source does not provide. 2030 identifies the limit of Monthey's transitional solution and the horizon indicated by ElCom for permanent capacity. item.title: Faster and more modern grids: Parliament accelerates the electric revolution
item.description: Over 60% of the very high voltage lines are close to the end of life; the threshold for overhead lines is 220 kV, while the distribution network involves voltages >36 kV and the new stations will not be able to exceed 20 m2 in surface area and 3 m in height.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Parliament and the Cantons have resolved the last divergence - Preference for overhead lines at 220 kV, except in certain cases - Over 60% of extra‑high‑voltage lines will reach end‑of‑life - The dossier is ready for final votes
## Key facts - Where → Bern - What → Revision of the Electricity Installations Act - Objective → Accelerate grid expansion - Threshold → 220 kV for preference of overhead lines - Distribution network → nominal voltage above 36 kV - Extra‑high‑voltage lines reaching end‑of‑life → over 60% - Transformation stations → maximum 20 m² and 3 metres - Dossier status → ready for final votes
Today, in Bern, the two chambers of Parliament reached an agreement on the revision of the Electricity Installations Act. The Cantons aligned with the National Council, clearing the last divergence. The dossier, devoted to accelerating expansion and simplifying grid transformation, is therefore ready for final votes.
### A grid to be expanded and renewed
The revision aims to support the energy transition by reducing bureaucratic delays and favouring grid efficiency. The dossier gives a two‑fold reason: the grid must meet growing demand while also being renewed. Over 60% of extra‑high‑voltage lines will reach end‑of‑life, while electricity line projects proliferate and authorisations take several years.
One central point concerns overhead lines. When voltage is equal to or greater than 220 kilovolts, preference will be given to them, except in certain cases. In buildable zones, lines may instead be buried. Parliament reintroduced the principle that the Federal Council had removed from the draft after strongly negative feedback from the consultation.
On the current route or in its immediate vicinity, existing high‑voltage lines may be replaced without a sectoral planning procedure. Parliament extended the rule to extra‑high‑voltage lines along national highways and railway lines, and to distribution‑network lines with a nominal voltage above 36 kV.
If pylons need to be moved, legal distances from forests and watercourses may be disregarded. Outside buildable zones, existing lines may be replaced even beyond the limits for noise and non‑ionising radiation, provided exposure does not increase further. Inside buildable zones, suitable measures must be verified to reduce it.
Transformation stations may also be built more easily outside buildable zones. They need not be directly adjacent to that zone: the ground footprint may not exceed 20 m² and the maximum height will be 3 metres. It will also be possible to replace or modify stations lawfully constructed outside buildable zones, provided no overriding interest opposes it. ## What changes when reading a project
For those who live or work near an electrical infrastructure, the difference does not lie in a single rule, but in the type of intervention. The revision distinguishes the replacement of existing lines from the expansion of the network and distinguishes the building zone from the area outside it. This framework makes it possible to understand where the text reduces a procedural step and where, instead, it maintains checks related to exposure.
### Before assessing a route
The first question is whether it concerns an existing line on the current route or in the immediate vicinity. For these replacements, the sectoral plan procedure is not required in the cases indicated by the revision. Parliament has also extended the principle to ultra-high-voltage lines along national roads and railway lines and to the distribution network with a nominal voltage above 36 kV.
The second question concerns the location. In building zones, undergrounding remains possible for lines with a voltage of 220 kV or more. Outside the building zone, existing lines may also be replaced beyond the noise and non-ionizing radiation limit values, but only if exposure does not increase further. Within the building zone, the text requires appropriate measures to reduce it to be verified. These are differences to check in the project.
| Situation to be verified | Criterion provided for by the text | |---|---| | Existing line on the route or in the immediate vicinity | Replacement without a sectoral plan procedure | | Building zone | Undergrounding of 220 kV lines possible | | Outside the building zone | Replacement beyond the limit values if exposure does not increase | | Transformer station | Outside the building zone, even if not adjacent; maximum 20 m2 and 3 metres |
The third key is the balancing of interests. Except in certain cases, a secure and economical energy supply will prevail over territorial protection and planning. The Federal Council intended to grant this overriding interest to the transmission network; Parliament extended it to the distribution network above 1 kV. The reader must therefore keep two aspects distinct: on the one hand, the security and cost-effectiveness of supply, and on the other, the territorial and exposure conditions laid down for the various interventions.

## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to read the dossier on your own area
A practical review can follow four steps. This is a way to apply the distinctions contained in the revision to the project's characteristics.
### Four checks
1. Classify the intervention. Check whether it concerns an existing line located on the current route or in the immediate vicinity, or a transformer substation. The simplification described by the source refers to the replacement of lines in the indicated cases and also allows stations legally built outside the building zone to be replaced or modified, when no overriding interest opposes this.
2. Identify the zone. Mark whether the location concerned is buildable or non-buildable. In the building zone, lines of 220 kV or more may be placed underground; outside the zone, an existing line may be replaced even beyond the limit values for noise and non-ionizing radiation, provided that exposure does not increase. Within the building zone, appropriate measures to reduce exposure must instead be verified.
3. Check the network and voltage. Note the indicated threshold: 220 kV for the preference for overhead lines, above 36 kV for the distribution network to which the simplification applies, and above 1 kV for the distribution network to which Parliament extended the overriding interest of a secure and economical supply. These are different reference points and must be read separately.
4. Verify the physical elements. For a transformer substation outside the building zone, check the ground area, which may not exceed 20 m2, and the maximum height of 3 meters. If the project moves the pylons, also consider the legal distances from forests and watercourses, which may not be observed.
This sequence makes it possible to move from the reform's general title to the detail affecting the individual facility: line or station, zone, voltage, exposure and dimensions. The next political step is represented by the final votes, for which the dossier is ready.

item.description: In August, Italian exports outside the EU grew by 16.1%: +57% to Switzerland, with gold bars indicated by ISTAT. Detailed data will come later.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Italian extra‑UE exports: +16.1% year‑on‑year - Switzerland: +57%, with gold bullions standing out - United States: +31.1%, with acceleration in pharmaceuticals - Istat: the detailed data will arrive later
## Key facts - Period → August - Area → extra‑UE countries - Overall growth → +16.1% year‑on‑year - Switzerland → +57% - United States → +31.1% - Leading goods → intermediate and capital goods - Switzerland → gold bullions - United States → pharmaceuticals
In August, Italian exports to extra‑UE countries recorded a strong year‑on‑year increase of +16.1%. The indication comes from the National Institute of Statistics, Istat, which in the press release highlights two destinations with marked increases: Switzerland, with +57%, and the United States, with +31.1%.
For Switzerland, the more specific reference is to gold bullions. The source does not yet present the full detail of the transactions: it states that the data will be published later. The available data therefore allows us to identify the category indicated by Istat, but not to establish quantities, absolute values or individual operators involved.
Istat attributes the growth of extra‑UE exports mainly to the rise in sales of intermediate and capital goods. The formulation refers to the general picture of Italian exports outside the European Union. The reference to gold bullions is instead linked in particular to the Swiss direction. For the United States, the press release signals an acceleration concerning pharmaceuticals.
### Three percentages, three perimeters
The reading must keep the three numbers separate. The 16.1% relates to the total of Italian exports to extra‑UE countries; the +57% refers to growth towards Switzerland; the +31.1% concerns growth towards the United States. These are three percentages with different scopes.
For those living in Switzerland, the national point of the news is the country’s role as a destination cited in the Italian data and the association with gold bullions. The press release does not describe effects on families, prices or Swiss incomes. Even the cost of living in Switzerland remains a different indicator: the Istat note talks about exports, not cost of living.
## The scope of the signal for Switzerland
The Italian data provides a precise signal about the direction of sales, but not a complete picture of the Swiss economy. The source links exports to Switzerland, in particular, to gold bars; however, it does not explain whether the growth depends on an increase in quantities, different unit values or a combination of elements. Without the detail announced by Istat, these hypotheses cannot be selected.
The same limitation applies to the national reading. The news does not indicate Swiss locations, operators, final recipients or the duration of the phenomenon. It does not attribute the growth to a political decision, a tax change, a customs rule or a change in prices. Including one of these elements would mean going beyond the press release.
### The correct comparison
It is instead possible to compare the overall non-EU scope with the two named destinations. The first measure describes the general trend; the other two isolate individual directions. The goods must also be kept distinct: intermediate and capital goods are the driver indicated for the whole, gold bars are the specific reference associated with Switzerland, and pharmaceuticals are the acceleration reported for the United States. This sequence cannot be turned into a complete ranking, because the text does not list all destinations or all categories.
For a Swiss reader, the practical consequence is a single, very concrete one: use the data to understand how the Swiss destination is described in the press release, not to estimate the impact on prices, incomes or consumption independently. Any currency comparison, when amounts become available, can be made with comparatore CHF/EUR, but the tool does not replace the Istat detail and does not convert a percentage into an absolute value.
This approach avoids two errors: reading the +57% as an already quantified sum of money, or presenting gold bars as the only export item to Switzerland. The source says that the category concerns those exports in particular, not that it accounts for the entire flow.

### A four-step procedure
For those who want to follow the data from the Swiss side, the operational step is to keep scope, destination, and goods separate. The source already indicates that the detail will arrive later: this is the only explicit timing milestone, so it must not be replaced with an invented deadline.
1. Start with the period: note that the communication concerns August. Every comparison must maintain the same period and the same annual basis indicated by Istat.
2. Separate the destinations: read the Switzerland line without transferring to it the data referring to the United States. The former is associated with gold bars; the latter with pharmaceuticals. This avoids attributing the pharmaceutical acceleration to Switzerland.
3. Await the detailed data: until they are published, record only the data already communicated and the category indicated. Do not add quantities, amounts, companies, locations, or reasons not present in the note.
4. Review the overall composition: verify how the detailed data fit in relation to intermediate goods and capital goods, which Istat identifies as the main driver of growth outside the EU. The reference to gold bars must not automatically be extended to all sales.
For a resident of Switzerland, this framework makes it possible to use the news without turning it into a personal forecast.
